name: Lash lift kit

image.caption: Lash lift v kozmetickom salóne Kambria

lead: A lash lift kit uses chemical solutions and silicone pads or rods to give natural lashes a semi-permanent upward curl that lasts several weeks. The payoff is eyes that look larger and more open without daily curling or mascara.

The chemistry resembles a hair perm: a reducing agent loosens keratin bonds, the lashes are shaped around a rod, and a neutralizer sets the new curl. It is offered in salons and as at-home kits. Published material consists of case reports and clinical commentary, including an optometry report on complaints of product reaching the eye; no trials of lash lifts were identified.

paras: People get it done in a salon or with a home kit, following the timing and patch-test steps in the instructions. The curl lasts until the lashes cycle out over several weeks, and many repeat it on that schedule. It is often combined with a lash tint or mascara.

Chemical irritation, allergic reactions and corneal injury have been reported, and allergens in lifts and tints persist until the lashes cycle out. Professionals have cautioned about home use near the eye. Patch testing and exact timing are the standard precautions.

chain: Eyes look larger and more open
angle.text: A lash lift perms natural lashes into an upward curl that lasts weeks, so the eyes look larger and more open without daily effort. It is done in salons and with at-home kits. Irritation near the eye is the main reported downside, so instructions are followed closely.

lead: A lash lift kit is a set of chemical solutions and silicone pads or rods used to give natural eyelashes a semi-permanent upward curl lasting several weeks. It is offered as a salon service and as at-home kits. The chemistry resembles a hair perm: a reducing agent loosens keratin bonds, the lashes are shaped on a rod, and a neutralizer sets them.

Evidence is limited to case reports and clinical commentary. An optometry report on cosmetic eye enhancements describes complaints of product reaching the eye, and case reports describe allergic and eye reactions to lash colouring. No trials of lash lifts were identified. [1][2]
infobox: Reduction and neutralization of keratin bonds

paras: Kits typically include lifting lotion, setting lotion, adhesive, pads or rods of various sizes and removal tools. Many kits also bundle lash tinting, so tint-related allergy reports apply to some products. [2]

A reducing agent breaks disulfide bonds in lash keratin, the lashes are moulded around a form, and a neutralizer re-forms the bonds in the curved position. The new shape persists until the lashes shed and are replaced.

Practitioners and consumers describe a curled, more open look without daily curling. This has not been tested in published trials. Consumer forum threads discuss the difficulty of doing the procedure at home. [3][4]

Optometric commentary reports chemical irritation, allergic reactions and corneal injury associated with cosmetic eye procedures, and professionals quoted there warn about home use. [1] A case report describes blepharoconjunctivitis due to chloro-PPD contact allergy after eyelash colouring, and the allergen can persist until treated lashes cycle out. [2] A case report of an open-globe injury from an eyelash curler illustrates mechanical hazards of related tools. [5]
Product instructions generally stress patch testing and following timing exactly.

The site rates the effect as strong but temporary and carries a note about irritation risk near the eyes. Discussion found online is mostly consumer beauty forums rather than appearance-optimization communities. [3][4]
No studies found on lash lift kits. Related reports are case reports of reactions to eyelash dye and of curler injury. [2][5]
